# Calibration — the committed synthetic corpus (synthetic, not the UEyes benchmark)

How human-like the attention engine currently is, measured against human gaze with the standard saliency and
scanpath metrics, against two baselines, per UI category and overall. An honest low number is better than a
flattering one.

> **These figures are measured over a synthetic stand-in corpus, not over UEyes.** The records are
> generated (#82) in the benchmark’s own shape so that this whole pipeline runs in CI with no download;
> they are not the benchmark’s screenshots and not its participants’ gaze. **No number in this report is a
> published UEyes score and none may be quoted as one.** Pointing the same code at the real dataset
> changes the data and not a line of the code, and this report will then name the dataset version it was
> measured on in its own heading.

### The map each predictor drew

| Predictor | Drawn from | Cell px | σ share | σ relative to | Truncation | Dwell weight | Normalisation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine` | fixations | 10 | 0.03 | map-longer-side | 3 | 1 | sum-to-one |
| `centre-bias-prior` | position-prior | 10 | 0.25 | image-shorter-side | whole-map | 0 | sum-to-one |
| `random-fixations` | fixations | 10 | 0.03 | map-longer-side | 3 | 1 | sum-to-one |

`engine` and `centre-bias-prior` drew their maps differently — `drawnFrom`, `sigmaShare`, `sigmaRelativeTo`, `truncationSigmas`, `dwellWeightExponent` — so a margin between them is placement **and** blur, and is read as both.

## What the product’s badge quotes

**The web category’s CC.** The header badge of every screen reads
`Simulated audience · gaze similarity 0.9` from the run artifact’s `calibration.cc`, which the
run loop writes from the engine’s own committed configuration. That is the **0.8965** in the
`webpage` row of the table below, over 1 record. The badge’s longer form names CC, NSS and
ScanMatch, all of that same category.

The web category is what this product is for (#11, user story 8) and is never folded into the overall mean: the
overall figures below cover four kinds of UI and are **not** what the badge is about. A run produced by an
engine that was never calibrated shows no number at all — the badge says so in words rather than printing a
zero.

## The objective and its weights

`web-cc-scanmatch` — the web category's CC plus ScanMatch, equally weighted. Scope: **webpage**, never the overall mean.

| Term | Weight | Figure | Contribution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CC | 0.5 | 0.8965 | 0.4483 |
| ScanMatch | 0.5 | 0.4144 | 0.2072 |
| **Objective** |  |  | **0.6555** |

Over 1 record of the `webpage` category. The two figures are not commensurable, so
the objective is a direction to climb and never a score to quote — `packages/calibration/docs/fitting.md` says
why, and the badge quotes CC itself rather than this sum.

## The margins

The engine minus each baseline, metric by metric, over the records both sides scored. A positive margin is
better on every metric but KLD, which is lower-is-better and so reads the other way. **A negative margin is a
reported result and not a failure**: the centre-bias prior is hard to beat on a saliency metric, and a report
that could only print a win would be decoration.

## The regression gate

`pnpm --filter @personavision/calibration run gate`
holds every figure above to the floor the measurement of **2026-10-27** recorded, which is the last row of
the history below. A figure that falls past its floor by more than its tolerance fails the gate; a figure that
rises past it is a result, not a failure, and is recorded by appending a row rather than by moving an earlier
one.

The tolerances exist for one reason: the figures are deterministic on one machine — `test/score.test.ts`
asserts two runs and two processes agree character for character — and the gate runs on another. CI is Linux on
x64 and these floors were measured on macOS on arm64, and the image decode and the sums after it are not
bit-identical across them. Each tolerance is at most a hundredth of the range its metric covers on this corpus,
which is orders of magnitude above that drift and far below the smallest regression worth catching: the
engine’s own defaults score 0.18 on web ScanMatch against the fitted 0.41, so a fit silently reverting would be
an eighteen-tolerance fall. `packages/calibration/src/report/render.ts` carries the same argument beside the
numbers, and a worker widening one has to replace it.

**What this gate holds, and what it does not — measured, not assumed.** Handing the fit back to the engine’s
defaults breaks floors in every scope, the web category’s ScanMatch among them by eighteen tolerances. So does
`gamma` at 0, which switches inhibition of return off, and `alpha` at 3, which makes the engine fixate the
single most salient area. Two searched parameters pass it untouched: `beta` at 0, because `predict` has no goal
and relevance is neutral there — which is what #90’s search space already says about that term — and `alpha` at
0.2, where the weight on salience is cut fivefold and no floor moves. That is the corpus’s limit and not the
tolerance’s: four records, one per category, so every per-category figure rests on a single record. The gate
will widen with the corpus rather than with an argument, and `test/regression.test.ts` pins each of these
sentences to a run.

| Metric | Tolerance | Read as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CC | 0.01 | fails when it falls past its floor minus the tolerance |
| NSS | 0.05 | fails when it falls past its floor minus the tolerance |
| KLD | 0.1 | fails when it rises past its floor plus the tolerance |
| AUC-Judd | 0.01 | fails when it falls past its floor minus the tolerance |
| ScanMatch | 0.01 | fails when it falls past its floor minus the tolerance |
| Sequence score | 0.01 | fails when it falls past its floor minus the tolerance |
